b.2a1c0b95d8:
<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Christus natus est nobis: * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Christus natus est nobis: * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro:
<r>Ant.</r> Christus natus est nobis: * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
<r>Ant.</r> Christus natus est nobis: * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Christus natus est nobis: * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Christus natus est nobis: * Veníte, adorémus.
b.fad12ef835:
<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Unto us a Christ is born, * O come, let us worship Him.
<r>Ant.</r> Unto us a Christ is born, * O come, let us worship Him.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour.
<r>Ant.</r> Unto us a Christ is born, * O come, let us worship Him.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us worship Him.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> Unto us a Christ is born, * O come, let us worship Him.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us worship Him.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> Unto us a Christ is born, * O come, let us worship Him.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us worship Him.
<r>Ant.</r> Unto us a Christ is born, * O come, let us worship Him.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
<r>Isa 9:1-6</r>
<n>1</n> Primo témpore alleviáta est terra Zábulon, et terra Néphthali: et novíssimo aggraváta est via maris trans Iordánem Galilǽæ géntium.
<n>2</n> Pópulus qui ambulábat in ténebris, vidit lucem magnam: habitántibus in regióne umbræ mortis, lux orta est eis.
<n>3</n> Multiplicásti gentem, et non magnificásti lætítiam. Lætabúntur coram te, sicut qui lætántur in messe, sicut exsúltant victóres, capta præda, quando dívidunt spólia.
<n>4</n> Iugum enim óneris eius, et virgam húmeri eius, et sceptrum exactóris eius superásti sicut in die Mádian.
<n>5</n> Quia omnis violénta prædátio cum tumúltu, et vestiméntum mistum sánguine, erit in combustiónem, et cibus ignis.
<n>6</n> Párvulus enim natus est nobis, et fílius datus est nobis, et factus est principátus super húmerum eius: et vocábitur nomen eius, Admirábilis, Consiliárius, Deus, Fortis, Pater futúri sǽculi, Princeps pacis.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Hódie nobis cælórum Rex de Vírgine nasci dignátus est, ut hóminem pérditum ad cæléstia regna revocáret: Gaudet exércitus Angelórum,
* Quia salus ætérna humáno géneri appáruit.
<r>℣.</r> Glória in excélsis Deo, et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis.
<r>℟.</r> Quia salus ætérna humáno géneri appáruit.

<h>Reading 1</h>
<r>Isa 9:1-6</r>
<n>1</n> At the first time the land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephtali was lightly touched: and at the last the way of the sea beyond the Jordan of the Galilee of the Gentiles was heavily loaded.
<n>2</n> The people that walked in darkness, have seen a great light: to them that dwelt in the region of the shadow of death, light is risen.
<n>3</n> Thou hast multiplied the nation, and hast not increased the joy. They shall rejoice before thee, as they that rejoice in the harvest, as conquerors rejoice after taking a prey, when they divide the spoils.
<n>4</n> For the yoke of their burden, and the rod of their shoulder, and the sceptre of their oppressor thou hast overcome, as in the day of Median.
<n>5</n> For every violent taking of spoils, with tumult, and garment mingled with blood, shall be burnt, and be fuel for the fire.
<n>6</n> For a child is born to us, and a son is given to us, and the government is upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called, Wonderful, Counsellor, God the Mighty, the Father of the world to come, the Prince of Peace.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> This is the day whereon the King of heaven was pleased to be born of a Virgin, that He might bring back to heaven man who was lost.
* There is joy among the hosts of Angels, because eternal salvation hath appeared unto men.
<r>℣.</r> Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, to men of goodwill.
* There is joy among the hosts of Angels, because eternal salvation hath appeared unto men.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>Isa 40:1-8</r>
<n>1</n> Consolámini, consolámini, pópule meus, dicit Deus vester.
<n>2</n> Loquímini ad cor Ierúsalem, et advocáte eam: quóniam compléta est malítia eius, dimíssa est iníquitas illíus: suscépit de manu Dómini duplícia pro ómnibus peccátis suis.
<n>3</n> Vox clamántis in desérto: Paráte viam Dómini, rectas fácite in solitúdine sémitas Dei nostri.
<n>4</n> Omnis vallis exaltábitur, et omnis mons et collis humiliábitur: et erunt prava in dirécta, et áspera in vias planas.
<n>5</n> Et revelábitur glória Dómini: et vidébit omnis caro páriter quod os Dómini locútum est.
<n>6</n> Vox dicéntis: Clama. Et dixi: Quid clamábo? Omnis caro fœnum, et omnis glória eius quasi flos agri.
<n>7</n> Exsiccátum est fœnum, et cécidit flos: quia spíritus Dómini sufflávit in eo. Vere fœnum est pópulus:
<n>8</n> Exsiccátum est fœnum, et cécidit flos: Verbum autem Dómini nostri manet in ætérnum.
<r>Isa 52:1-6</r>
<n>1</n> Consúrge, consúrge, indúere fortitúdine tua, Sion, indúere vestiméntis glóriæ tuæ, Ierúsalem, cívitas sancti: quia non adíciet ultra ut pertránseat per te incircumcísus, et immúndus.
<n>2</n> Excútere de púlvere, consúrge, sede, Ierúsalem: solve víncula colli tui, captíva fília Sion.
<n>3</n> Quia hæc dicit Dóminus: Gratis venumdáti estis, et sine argénto redimémini.
<n>4</n> Quia hæc dicit Dóminus Deus: In Ægýptum descéndit pópulus meus in princípio, ut colónus esset ibi: et Assur absque ulla causa calumniátus est eum.
<n>5</n> Et nunc quid mihi est hic, dicit Dóminus, quóniam ablátus est pópulus meus gratis? Dominatóres eius iníque agunt, dicit Dóminus: et iúgiter tota die nomen meum blasphemátur.
<n>6</n> Propter hoc sciet pópulus meus nomen meum, in die illa: quia ego ipse qui loquébar, ecce adsum.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Descéndit de cælis Deus verus a Patre génitus, † introívit in úterum Vírginis, nobis ut apparéret visíbilis, indútus carne humána protoparénte édita: Et exívit per portam clausam † Deus et homo,
* Lux et vita, cónditor mundi.
<r>℣.</r> Tamquam sponsus † Dóminus procédens de thálamo suo.
<r>℟.</r> Lux et vita, cónditor mundi.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<r>Isa 40:1-8</r>
<n>1</n> Be comforted, be comforted, my people, saith your God.
<n>2</n> Speak ye to the heart of Jerusalem, and call to her: for her evil is come to an end, her iniquity is forgiven: she hath received of the hand of the Lord double for all her sins.
<n>3</n> The voice of one crying in the desert: Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make straight in the wilderness the paths of our God.
<n>4</n> Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low, and the crooked shall become straight, and the rough ways plain.
<n>5</n> And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh together shall see, that the mouth of the Lord hath spoken.
<n>6</n> The voice of one, saying: Cry. And I said: What shall I cry? All flesh is grass, and all the glory thereof as the flower of the field.
<n>7</n> The grass is withered, and the flower is fallen, because the spirit of the Lord hath blown upon it. Indeed the people is grass:
<n>8</n> The grass is withered, and the flower is fallen: but the word of our Lord endureth for ever.
<r>Isa 52:1-6</r>
<n>1</n> Arise, arise, put on thy strength, O Sion, put on the garments of thy glory, O Jerusalem, the city of the Holy One: for henceforth the uncircumcised, and unclean shall no more pass through thee.
<n>2</n> Shake thyself from the dust, arise, sit up, O Jerusalem: loose the bonds from off thy neck, O captive daughter of Sion.
<n>3</n> For thus saith the Lord: You were sold gratis, and you shall be redeemed without money.
<n>4</n> For thus saith the Lord God: My people went down into Egypt at the beginning to sojourn there: and the Assyrian hath oppressed them without any cause at all.
<n>5</n> And now what have I here, saith the Lord: for my people is taken away gratis. They that rule over them treat them unjustly, saith the Lord, and my name is continually blasphemed all the day long.
<n>6</n> Therefore my people shall know my name in that day: for I myself that spoke, behold I am here.
<h>H</h>æc dicit Dóminus Deus: Convertímini ad me, et salvi éritis.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> He came down from heaven: true God, begotten of the Father: he entered the Virgin's womb, that he might be made clearly manifest to us, clothed in human flesh put forth by the Creator,
* He went out through the closed door, God and man, Light and Life, Author of the world.
<r>℣.</r> Like a bridegroom, the Lord coming forth from his chamber.
<r>℟.</r> Author of the world.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Lucam
<r>Luc 2:33-40</r>
<c>I</c>n illo témpore: Erat Ioseph, et María mater Iesu, mirántes super his, quæ dicebántur de illo. Et réliqua.

Homilía sancti Ambrósii Epíscopi
<r>Lib. 2 in cap. 2 Lucæ, prope finem</r>
<c>V</c>ides úberem in omnes grátiam, Dómini generatióne diffúsam, et prophetíam incrédulis negátam esse, non iustis. Ecce et Símeon prophétat, in ruínam et resurrectiónem plurimórum venísse Dóminum Iesum Christum, ut iustórum, iniquorúmque mérita discérnat; et pro nostrórum qualitáte factórum, iudex verus et iustus aut supplícia decérnat, aut prǽmia. Et tuam ipsíus ánimam pertransíbit gládius.

<r>℟.</r> Verbum caro factum est, et habitávit in nobis: cuius glóriam vídimus, quasi Unigéniti a Patre,
* Plenum grátiæ et veritátis.
<r>℣.</r> In princípio erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum.
<r>℟.</r> Plenum grátiæ et veritátis.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Plenum grátiæ et veritátis.

<r>Te Deum</r>
<c>T</c>e Deum laudámus: * te Dóminum confitémur.
Te ætérnum Patrem * omnis terra venerátur.

b.b275fabd58:
<h>Capitulum Hymnus Versus</h>
<r>Heb 1:1-2</r>
<c>M</c>ultifáriam, multísque modis olim Deus loquens pátribus in prophétis: novíssime diébus istis locútus est nobis in Fílio, quem constítuit herédem universórum, per quem fecit et sǽcula.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>V</c>eni, redémptor géntium,
Osténde partum Vírginis:
Mirétur omne sæculum:
Talis decet partus Deum.

<h>N</h>on ex viríli sémine,
Sed mýstico spirámine
Verbum Dei factum est caro
Fructúsque ventris flóruit.

<h>A</h>lvus tuméscit Vírginis,
Claustrum pudóris pérmanet,
Vexílla virtútum micant,
Versátur in templo Deus.

<h>P</h>rocédat e thálamo suo,
Pudóris aula régia,
Géminæ gigas substántiæ
Alácris ut currat viam.

<h>Æ</h>quális ætérno Patri,
Carnis tropæo cíngere,
Infírma nostri córporis
Virtúte firmans pérpeti.

<h>P</h>ræsépe iam fulget tuum
Luménque nox spirat novum,
Quod nulla nox intérpolet
Fidéque iugi lúceat.

<h>G</h>lória tibi, Dómine,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et Sancto Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Verbum caro factum est, allelúia.
<r>℟.</r> Et habitávit in nobis, allelúia.
